messages:
alyssa: Quick question — we're migrating postgres creds to ExternalSecrets + CSI driver. Goal: per-namespace conditional key mapping (prod uses postfix -prod), and short TTL-based refresh for rotated creds. Anyone seen weird edge cases?

michael: fyi we've done namespace-scoped mapping before. Main gotcha: ExternalSecrets templates vs. CSI provider naming differs. Post the YAML you're trying?

alyssa: Here's a trimmed ExternalSecret we're testing:
```yaml
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: pg-credentials
  namespace: staging
spec:
  refreshInterval: 1m
  secretStoreRef:
    name: vault-store
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
  target:
    name: pg-credentials
    template:
      type: Opaque
      data:
        connection: .data.connection_string
  data:
  - secretKey: username
    remoteRef:
      key: secret/data/db/staging/postgres
      property: username
  - secretKey: password
    remoteRef:
      key: secret/data/db/staging/postgres
      property: password
```

jin: Couple notes: 1) refreshInterval 1m is aggressive — will cause lots of Vault reads on mass rollout. 2) If you want namespace-based postfixing, the CSI driver creates files by key name, but ExternalSecrets target.template.name needs to incorporate namespace via controller features (some controllers support `{{ .Namespace }}` in name templates). Which ES operator/version?

alyssa: We're on external-secrets/operator 0.6.1. I read name templating was added but unsure if supported for ClusterSecretStore-backed items.

michael: operator 0.6.x has templating but ClusterSecretStore should be fine. For postfixing you can do target.template.name: "pg-credentials-{{ .Namespace }}" then map expected key names in your app. Alternative is keep secret name same and use K8s service account + env var to pick namespace-specific DB host.

carol: Also watch RBAC: when switching to CSI, the operator needs permission to create SecretProviderClass or mount CSI volume for each namespace. Our terraform change required a rolebinding patch:
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_role_binding" "es_csi_bind" {
  metadata {
    name = "external-secrets-csi-bind"
    namespace = each.value
  }
  role_ref {
    api_group = "rbac.authorization.k8s.io"
    kind = "ClusterRole"
    name = "external-secrets-operator"
  }
  subject {
    kind = "ServiceAccount"
    name = "external-secrets"
    namespace = "external-secrets-system"
  }
}
```

jin: For TTL-driven rotation: Vault-side leases + ExternalSecrets refreshInterval is good, but prefer external webhook-based rotation signal if you want immediate rotation on credential change. Otherwise you'll have the refresh window. Also defensively add backoff and jitter to avoid thundering herd.

alyssa: Good call. We don't need immediate, just want lower exposure. I'll bump refreshInterval to 5m and set backoff jitter in the operator config.

michael: small ops checklist before rollout:
- Verify operator version on prod cluster
- Terraform apply for rolebindings in all namespaces (use for_each)
- Smoke test with staging secret + helm chart that mounts CSI
- Monitor Vault read QPS during test

infra-bot: terraform-plan: success for module/k8s-secrets (plan id: plan-9876) :white_check_mark:

alyssa: Thanks all — I'll open the TF PR and ping for review. @michael @jin can you glance when it's up? :thumbsup:

michael: yup, will review.

jin: ping me after PR, I'll sanity-check RBAC and jitter settings.
